subject: Order form negotiation: liability allocation for regulatory fines and third-party claim recovery
messages:
From: Jack Morrison <jack.morrison@finovo.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Order form — regulatory fines, PCI/GDPR treatment

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement at Finovo is prepping the PO but they flagged the liability section in the Order Form and want clarity on how regulatory fines (GDPR/CCPA) and PCI penalties are treated under the Limitation of Liability.

High level asks from procurement/DPO:
- Are regulatory fines excluded from the cap or carved out only where Redwood is at fault?
- Will Redwood accept subrogation / recovery assistance if Finovo is assessed a fine related to Redwood-held logs or processing?
- Does Redwood maintain cyber liability or PI insurance that would respond to fines/penalties? If so, limits and carriers?

I attached our security questionnaire (partial) that highlights the procurement concern. Can you confirm Redwood's current position so we can move forward?

Jack Morrison
Head of Procurement
Finovo Payments

Attachment: Finovo_Security_Questionnaire_v3.pdf

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Jack Morrison <jack.morrison@finovo.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form — regulatory fines, PCI/GDPR treatment

Hi Jack — thanks for the note and the questionnaire. Looping in Neha (Legal) and Marcus (Sales Ops) to help.

Short answer: Redwood does not accept a blanket exclusion of regulatory fines from the cap. We treat fines/penalties differently depending on cause:
- If fines result directly from Redwood's breach of our written data processing obligations (e.g., a service-side vulnerability that caused unauthorized disclosure of customer personal data), we are prepared to agree that such regulatory fines are not subject to the monetary cap (i.e., carveout) and to cooperate on regulatory response and subrogation assistance.
- We cannot accept responsibility for fines that arise from the customer's misconfiguration, use of the service outside documented parameters, or from third-party integrations controlled by the customer — those should remain excluded from Redwood liability.

Proposed approach for the order form:
- Preserve the standard aggregate liability cap (greater of $X or fees over 12 months).
- Add a narrowly tailored carveout for regulatory fines and statutory penalties that are caused by Redwood's violation of its security and data processing obligations.
- Require reasonable cooperation and a limited subrogation pathway (Redwood may seek recovery from a third party where appropriate).

I'll attach a marked-up draft of the Order Form with suggested language. If Finovo needs full exclusion or additional insurance requirements, please confirm and we'll evaluate escalation to Commercial and Legal leadership.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call on Wednesday to run through the redlines?

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_orderform_markedup.docx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jack Morrison <jack.morrison@finovo.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form — regulatory fines, PCI/GDPR treatment

Jack / Sofia / team — quick legal note and proposed clause text.

We want to keep the language tight and operationally testable. Proposed carveout snippet (for redline):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing limitation of liability, Redwood shall remain liable for regulatory fines, statutory penalties, and similar governmental assessments to the extent such amounts arise directly from Redwood's failure to comply with its obligations under the Data Processing Addendum or material breach of the Order Form. Redwood's aggregate liability for all other Claims shall remain subject to the Cap. Redwood's liability for regulatory fines shall be limited to those amounts finally adjudicated or agreed in settlement, and Redwood shall have the right to contest, mitigate, and seek contribution/subrogation from responsible third parties where appropriate."

Additional points:
- For PCI-specific fines assessed as a result of the customer's failure to follow cardholder-data handling instructions, those should remain the customer's responsibility unless Redwood's confirmed control-plane breach is the proximate cause.
- We can provide insurance information (carrier and limits) on a reciprocal NDA basis. We do carry cyber/PI insurance with limits sufficient for enterprise customers but cannot guarantee full coverage for regulatory penalties in all jurisdictions.

Attachment: proposed_liability_snippet.txt

If Finovo pushes for a full exclusion of fines from the cap, we'll need to evaluate premium concessions or a carveout to require higher minimum liability or an insurance/indemnity swap. Happy to discuss on a call.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Jack Morrison <jack.morrison@finovo.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Finovo DPO <dpo@finovo.com>, procurement@finovo.com
Date: 2026-12-03T14:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form — regulatory fines, PCI/GDPR treatment

Neha — thanks for the clarity. Procurement and the DPO are pushing back: Finovo can't accept language that leaves regulatory fines inside the cap unless there is a clear insurance response or an express indemnity for statutory fines. Our position:
- Regulatory fines (GDPR/CCPA) and card network PCI penalties must be excluded from any liability cap.
- Redwood should either warranty appropriate cyber liability insurance with defined minimum limits or accept a narrow indemnity for regulatory fines resulting from Redwood's processing.
- We also need commitment on cooperation (forensics, notifications) and a commitment not to assert subrogation against Finovo without prior approval.

Attached are our counter redlines. If Redwood cannot accept the exclusion, we will need to identify offsetting commercial concessions (extended term, price credits, or guaranteed incident response SLA).

Jack Morrison
Head of Procurement
Finovo Payments

Attachment: finovo_counter_redlines.docx

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Jack Morrison <jack.morrison@finovo.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form — regulatory fines, PCI/GDPR treatment

Jack — appreciate the clarity and the redlines. Next steps from our side:

1) Sales/legal posture for negotiation
- Redwood will propose the narrow carveout for regulatory fines caused by Redwood's breach, plus an explicit cooperation and remediation commitment.
- If Finovo requires a full exclusion, Redwood would need commercial offsets: either a higher liability cap (mutual agreement on a higher dollar cap), insurance confirmation (carrier and minimum limits), or a one-time commercial concession.

2) Action items
- Marcus: please prep two commercial scenarios (1) standard carveout + cooperation, (2) full exclusion with commercial offsets (pricing/term/credits).
- Neha: prepare a clean redline we can share on the call that includes proposed insurance language and the subrogation/consent mechanics.
- Jack/Finovo: please confirm availability for a 30-minute negotiation call — propose Thursday 10–10:30 AM CET.

Related links: DocuSign order draft (https://redwood.app/docusign/FNVO-ORDER-ABC123), HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/FNVO-1298).

If we can't land the posture in this call, we should escalate to Commercial Leadership (Lauren and Marcus to coordinate).

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
